mortality.value: Described as a major cause of death in laying hens; a 2019 study found 74% of caged-hen deaths were from this condition versus only 0-5% in cage-free/free-range hens
A leading noninfectious cause of death in backyard chickens; birds are typically found dead suddenly

diagnosis.value: Confirmed at necropsy by finding an enlarged, pale, fat-laden liver with hemorrhage

treatment_overview.value: Because death is often sudden, treatment options are limited; management focuses on controlling energy intake and body weight along with vitamin and mineral supplementation to prevent the condition

when_to_call_vet.value: An overweight caged hen with pale comb and dropping egg production should be evaluated, since fatty liver hemorrhagic syndrome often causes sudden unexpected death with few warning signs.

summary.value: Fatty liver hemorrhagic syndrome is a metabolic condition in which excess dietary energy and limited exercise cause too much fat to build up in a hen's liver, making it prone to sudden, often fatal internal bleeding. It mostly affects overweight, high-producing laying hens and is managed by controlling diet and body weight rather than by treatment after the fact.
